editorial_note: This archive uses the Chinese People's War of Resistance Against Japanese Aggression as learning context. Character relationships, combined place names and individual operations in the game include artistic invention and do not replace textbooks, archives or scholarship.

missions.title: Mission 1: Rescue Operation
missions.period: War of Resistance, behind enemy lines · Rescue in occupied territory
missions.historical_context: Resistance forces behind enemy lines often relied on civilian shelter, couriers and small detachments to rescue prisoners. Concealed approach, reconnaissance and civilian protection mattered more than simply eliminating enemy troops.
missions.objective_context: Rescue Peng Xin and Uncle Luo and move them out of danger. The mission emphasizes task priority, protection of people and avoiding needless combat.
missions.fact_vs_fiction: Behind-the-lines rescue and civilian support have a real historical basis; the names, village layout, garrison and events in this mission are fictionalized.

people.name: Courier
people.note: Couriers carried intelligence, maintained contacts and guided units; exposure could endanger an entire network.

places.name: Village in occupied territory
places.note: Villages could provide concealment but also became dangerous under checkpoints and patrols.

weapons.name: Broadsword and pistol
weapons.note: Quiet close-range weapons reduce noise, but demand careful approach and timing.

events.name: Rescue behind enemy lines
events.note: Resistance soldiers and civilians used many methods to recover wounded people, cadres and detained civilians.

missions.optional_challenge: Complete the mission without an alarm or any squad loss.

missions.title: Mission 2: Raid on the Train Station
missions.period: War of Resistance, behind enemy lines · Transport-line sabotage
missions.historical_context: Railways were crucial for moving enemy troops, supplies and plundered goods. Resistance forces combined reconnaissance, disguise and small raids with larger operations.
missions.objective_context: Obtain a uniform, rescue the driver, destroy the barracks targets and withdraw by train as one connected disguise, rescue, demolition and escape plan.
missions.fact_vs_fiction: Railway sabotage was widespread; the station, timetable, use of the uniform and personal stories are artistic invention.

people.name: Railway worker
people.note: Workers' knowledge of track, locomotives and dispatch made them important sources of technical help and intelligence.

places.name: Military railway station
places.note: Such sites combined checkpoints, warehouses, barracks and dispatch facilities under dense guard.

weapons.name: Demolition charge
weapons.note: A real operation must control placement and withdrawal time while protecting noncombatants.

events.name: Transport-line campaigns
events.note: Damaging railways and roads could delay enemy supply and troop movement.

missions.optional_challenge: Finish within ten minutes without losing a squad member.

missions.title: Mission 3: Prison Break
missions.period: War of Resistance, behind enemy lines · Rescue and sabotage
missions.historical_context: Occupation authorities used prisons, strongpoints and transport units to control local communities. Prison rescues often required coordination inside and outside while cutting off reinforcements.
missions.objective_context: Rescue Qiangzi, destroy the supply truck and withdraw. Success depends on route planning, objective order and escape timing.
missions.fact_vs_fiction: Rescuing detainees and intercepting military transport have historical precedents; the prison, characters and operation are a fictional combination.

people.name: Detained resistance member
people.note: People under interrogation still bore responsibility for protecting their organization and intelligence.

places.name: Enemy prison
places.note: Doors, checkpoints and patrol routes determine the difficulty of a rescue.

weapons.name: Rifle
weapons.note: A rifle has useful range, but its report exposes the shooter's position.

events.name: Resistance to pacification campaigns
events.note: Communities resisted searches and blockades through evacuation, communications and counteraction.

missions.optional_challenge: Complete the rescue using no more than five attacks.

missions.title: Mission 4: Railway Bridge
missions.period: War of Resistance, behind enemy lines · Railway-bridge sabotage
missions.historical_context: Bridges were critical railway nodes. Their destruction could interrupt transport longer than damage to ordinary track, but required exact reconnaissance, charge placement and timely withdrawal.
missions.objective_context: Place charges at key points on the bridge and leave by vehicle. Victory requires a complete demolition-and-withdrawal chain, not elimination of the whole garrison.
missions.fact_vs_fiction: Bridge and railway attacks were common behind enemy lines; this bridge, its guards and the escape vehicle were designed for play.

people.name: Demolition specialist
people.note: A specialist identified structural weak points and managed placement and safe withdrawal.

places.name: Railway bridge
places.note: Piers, abutments and track connections could all be critical targets.

weapons.name: Timed explosives
weapons.note: Use requires a safe distance and a planned withdrawal window.

events.name: Transport sabotage during the Hundred Regiments Offensive
events.note: The 1940 campaign attacked railways, roads and strongpoints on a large scale; this mission is not a reconstruction of one action.

missions.optional_challenge: Withdraw without triggering a global alarm.

missions.title: Mission 5: Burning the Granaries
missions.period: War of Resistance, behind enemy lines · Resisting plunder and disrupting supplies
missions.historical_context: Occupation forces requisitioned and seized grain and built military depots. Protecting civilian food and disrupting enemy supply were important parts of resistance behind enemy lines.
missions.objective_context: Rescue Guming, eliminate the officer, recover the plan and destroy the granaries, establishing an intelligence advantage before attacking personnel and supplies.
missions.fact_vs_fiction: Resistance to plunder and attacks on military storage have historical foundations; the granaries, people and plan in this mission are fictional.

people.name: Village informant
people.note: An informant could observe garrison and supply movements while maintaining an everyday identity.

places.name: Military grain depot
places.note: A requisitioned depot was both a supply node and a threat to nearby civilian subsistence.

weapons.name: Incendiary and demolition equipment
weapons.note: The game simplifies their use; real action must assess fire spread and risk to civilians.

events.name: Resistance to economic blockade
events.note: Base areas relied on production, transport and anti-plunder efforts to sustain soldiers and civilians.

missions.optional_challenge: Reach 80% accuracy without losing a squad member.

missions.title: Mission 6: Havoc in Hanjiang Town
missions.period: War of Resistance, behind enemy lines · Counter-espionage and intelligence recovery
missions.historical_context: Collaborationist administrations used agents, informant networks and coercion to control communities. Underground organizations had to verify intelligence, protect civilians and deal with saboteurs under discipline.
missions.objective_context: Identify and eliminate the traitor and recover the document, distinguishing the target from ordinary people and preserving the intelligence.
missions.fact_vs_fiction: Counter-espionage and protection of underground routes are historical contexts; Hanjiang Town, the target and the document are fictional.

people.name: Underground worker
people.note: Underground workers balanced intelligence collection with the safety of contacts and civilians.

places.name: Occupied market town
places.note: Dense streets supported concealment but also checkpoints, agents and rapid alarm spread.

weapons.name: Close-combat weapon
weapons.note: Quiet action can limit alarm spread but requires positive identification and control.

events.name: Counter-espionage behind enemy lines
events.note: Resistance organizations protected communications and investigated hostile networks.

missions.optional_challenge: Recover the document without triggering an alarm.

missions.title: Mission 7: Retribution
missions.period: War of Resistance, behind enemy lines · Surveillance and targeted action
missions.historical_context: Action against important enemy or collaborationist personnel required reliable intelligence and an unambiguous target. Following contacts, identification and escape planning reduced the risk of harming the wrong people.
missions.objective_context: Follow the contact, confirm the meeting, deal with Sun and Kato in order, and leave the area. Observation and withdrawal matter as much as the attack.
missions.fact_vs_fiction: Reconnaissance and action against enemy and collaborationist personnel occurred behind the lines; the names, meeting and pursuit are fictionalized.

people.name: Contact under surveillance
people.note: A contact's movement can reveal a network, but premature action can destroy the intelligence trail.

places.name: Clandestine meeting area
places.note: Approach and escape routes are central to a covert meeting site's risk.

weapons.name: Concealable weapon
weapons.note: A compact weapon aids concealment but does not replace target verification.

events.name: Targeted operations
events.note: Such operations depended on intelligence, discipline and plans to protect surrounding civilians.

missions.optional_challenge: Lose no squad members and trigger no more than one alarm.

missions.title: Mission 8: Breakout
missions.period: War of Resistance, behind enemy lines · Civilian protection and evacuation
missions.historical_context: During sweeps, blockades and searches, moving civilians and important personnel to safety was central work behind enemy lines. An escort moved slowly and needed forward reconnaissance.
missions.objective_context: Rescue the parents and reporter, then evacuate everyone. The player must manage the speed and safety of combatants and noncombatants together.
missions.fact_vs_fiction: Civilian evacuation and protection of journalists fit the historical setting; the family, reporter and route are fictional.

people.name: War correspondent
people.note: Reporters documented the war under dangerous conditions and depended on local protection and guidance.

places.name: Blocked evacuation route
places.note: Patrols and checkpoints could turn a familiar road into a hazardous corridor.

weapons.name: Covering fire
weapons.note: Fire should support withdrawal rather than expose an escort to unnecessary battle.

events.name: Civilian evacuation
events.note: Communities organized concealment and movement during enemy sweeps and blockades.

missions.optional_challenge: Evacuate everyone alive within twelve minutes.

missions.title: Mission 9: Shadow War in the Mine
missions.period: War of Resistance, behind enemy lines · Resource sabotage
missions.historical_context: Occupation forces exploited coal, minerals and industry to sustain war. Enclosed, complex mines made sabotage especially dependent on worker safety and escape routes.
missions.objective_context: Place charges, detonate them deliberately and leave by elevator. Each step has a strict order.
missions.fact_vs_fiction: Resistance to resource plunder and industrial sabotage have historical contexts; the mine, charge points and elevator sequence were designed for the game.

people.name: Mine worker
people.note: Workers understood underground structures and faced direct danger from occupation and sabotage.

places.name: Occupied mine
places.note: Confined passages complicate reconnaissance, blast safety and evacuation.

weapons.name: Placed explosives
weapons.note: Sequencing and a safe evacuation route are essential in enclosed terrain.

events.name: Resistance to resource plunder
events.note: Communities and resistance forces opposed the extraction of strategic resources.

missions.optional_challenge: Reach 80% accuracy and evacuate every squad member by elevator.

missions.title: Mission 10: Treasure Raiders
missions.period: War of Resistance, behind enemy lines · Document recovery and train sabotage
missions.historical_context: Military documents could reveal transport, deployment and requisition plans. Destroying transport after recovering intelligence could turn information into an immediate battlefield advantage.
missions.objective_context: Recover the documents, secure the key station area and destroy the train, switching between reconnaissance, area control and demolition.
missions.fact_vs_fiction: Capturing documents and sabotaging military trains have historical precedents; the treasure label, documents and station battle are fictional.

people.name: Enemy staff officer
people.note: Orders and handover papers carried by officers could expose wider logistics and command arrangements.

places.name: Temporary military station
places.note: A temporary station could still concentrate guards, supplies and vulnerable rolling stock.

weapons.name: Train demolition charge
weapons.note: Multiple targets require careful distribution of charges and escape time.

events.name: Military-train sabotage
events.note: Rail attacks sought to interrupt the movement of arms, troops and supplies.

missions.optional_challenge: Finish within ten minutes with no more than one alarm.

missions.title: Mission 11: Bloodied Ferry
missions.period: War of Resistance, behind enemy lines · Contest for a river crossing
missions.historical_context: Ferries were crucial movement points in river regions. Controlling high ground, covering a crossing and blocking reinforcements could decide a local operation.
missions.objective_context: Coordinate split groups to seize and hold the high ground, managing spacing, fire coverage and simultaneous arrival.
missions.fact_vs_fiction: Fighting for crossings and high ground is common in warfare; the location, units and deployment are artistic invention.

people.name: Ferry guide
people.note: Local knowledge of banks, currents and roads could determine a safe crossing.

places.name: River ferry and high ground
places.note: High ground overlooking a crossing controls observation and fire routes.

weapons.name: Rifle fire team
weapons.note: Separated teams need timing and mutual support rather than isolated attacks.

events.name: Contests for crossings
events.note: Crossings repeatedly became critical points for movement, withdrawal and supply.

missions.optional_challenge: Lose no squad members and achieve at least 85% accuracy.

missions.title: Mission 12: Airfield Sabotage
missions.period: War of Resistance, behind enemy lines · Airfield sabotage
missions.historical_context: Military airfields supported reconnaissance, bombing and transport. Attacking one was high risk and usually required long reconnaissance, coordination and withdrawal before a full enemy response.
missions.objective_context: Eliminate the commander, destroy key airfield facilities and withdraw northwest, combining reconnaissance, combat, demolition and escape.
missions.fact_vs_fiction: Reconnaissance, harassment and sabotage against airfields and aviation facilities occurred during the war; this airfield, commander and result do not reconstruct one specific battle.

people.name: Airfield commander
people.note: Command personnel coordinated guards, aircraft operation and emergency response.

places.name: Military airfield
places.note: Aircraft, towers, fuel stores and approach roads formed a defended system of targets.

weapons.name: Demolition and incendiary equipment
weapons.note: Different facilities require different placement while fuel stores create severe secondary hazards.

events.name: Raids on aviation facilities
events.note: Resistance forces gathered intelligence on and sometimes attacked airfields and related infrastructure.

missions.optional_challenge: Finish within fifteen minutes without losing a squad member.
